purpose: Persistent projection of LBE authority, evidence-gated progression, and the Rust/Ratatui TUI client integration. Mature upstream agent/runtime/TUI capabilities must be reused or adapted before any new implementation is created. Canonical LBE repository/runtime evidence remains authoritative.
authority_rule: Current workspace/runtime evidence and canonical machine governance outrank this projection. GPT-Knowledge never creates runtime truth or implementation authority.
core_doctrine: Provider/agent reasons. LBE governs. Reuse mature mechanics before rebuilding them. Registered capabilities execute through LBE. Evidence and ToolReceipts persist. Validation decides completion. Interfaces project the result.

product_identity.authority_rule: The TUI, Cline, and OpenCode cannot replace LBE policy, authorization, governed execution, receipt, evidence, persistence, validation or completion owners.

truth_model.acceptance: what happened for a bounded slice
truth_model.conflict_rule: When these disagree, classify the conflict or uncertainty; do not guess.

machine_gate.rule: Do not derive current gate state from this projection. Read the canonical LBE machine gate before authorizing further implementation.

owners: workspace/session identity where defined by LBE contracts

reuse_first_policy.rule: Before implementing any remaining capability, determine whether the canonical LBE runtime already owns it, whether Cline already provides reusable mechanics, or whether OpenCode provides reusable/adaptable runtime or TUI behavior. BUILD_NEW is permitted only after those checks fail or are explicitly rejected by the LBE authority boundary.

native terminal interaction patterns where applicable
cline.boundary: Executable filesystem/process/Git/external actions must cross LBE authorization and governed dispatch. Cline-native mutation/approval defaults are not LBE authority.

opencode.role: open-source reuse/adaptation source for TUI, client/server, provider, permission, MCP, agent/subagent and headless patterns
opencode.boundary: OpenCode is a reference/reuse source, not execution authority. Current-source capability-by-capability audit is still required before claiming direct reuse.
